quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?

options.text: Always ride in a staggered formation.

questions.explanation: Usually, groups ride best in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How should passengers hold on?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Do not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to grip your hips, waist, or belt firmly. They can also hold onto secure handholds if available.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control the motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need?
questions.explanation: Always keep enough space to stop safely based on road conditions. Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, what must you do?
questions.explanation: Shift into higher gears as your motorcycle speeds up.

questions.question: When other vehicles are stopped or moving slowly, what should you do?

options.text: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is okay to weave in and out of traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or objects may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Watch for what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches what other road users do and predicts problems. This helps you stay alert and ready for anything.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing any time you ride.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: White signs with red and black markings show traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When can you shift gears while turning?

options.text: Only if you can shift smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the turn.
It is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you can shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can cause the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing to be more visible, even in daylight. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should check all of the following, except:

options.text: A test of the turn signals.

questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands before riding.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: If parked cars are on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to avoid car doors opening and pedestrians stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while keeping enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: Pointed with your toes aiming downward.

questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, you can see bumps ahead by:

options.text: Listening for the other vehicle scraping against the pavement.
Noticing the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
Looking at the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead and trying to determine if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Noticing the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the taillights of the vehicle ahead. If they bounce up and down, bumps are on the road.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before a turn. Shifting during a turn can cause a sudden power change that makes the rear wheel skid. If you must shift during a turn, shift smoothly.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the impact.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your leg joints absorb some of the shock. This keeps the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards every time you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A working clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When riding in rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get better traction.

questions.question: If you have one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills are affected by even the first drink. Do not ride if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: To prevent collisions, a rider should:

options.text: Look straight ahead of the motorcycle.
Refuse to move to avoid hazards.
Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road 10 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Where is conflict between you and other vehicles most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles are most likely to occur at intersections.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.
